newsitem.title: UK: Ernst & Young reveals British financial data.
newsitem.headline: Ernst & Young reveals British financial data.

text.p: International accounting and consulting partnership Ernst & Young said Tuesday it made a profit of $125.4 million in Britain, revealing financial details of its operations for the first time.
The 21 percent rise in profits in the year to June 30 was made on gross fee income of 456 million British pounds ($761 million) and represented a 17 percent rise in average profit per partner.

Ernst & Young's senior partner Nick Land also confirmed that the firm was still planning to become a limited liability partnership registered in the Channel Island of Jersey despite the fact that the government has said it intends to introduce legislation recognising partnerships of this kind in Britain.
Land also said that Ernst & Young's worlwide revenue for the year to September would show a 13 percent rise to $7.8 billion.

Ernst & Young is the world's largest tax accounting practice and the second largest management consulting firm after Arthur Andersen. It was formed in 1989 from the merger of Ernst & Whinney and Arthur Young.
